# Abacus Global Management and Retirable Announce Partnership, Integrating Abacus LifeARC™ into Retirable Platform


October 13, 2026 8:00am EDT


*Abacus clients will gain a direct path to personalized retirement planning*


ORLANDO, Fla. & NEW YORK--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Abacus Global Management, Inc. (NYSE: ABX) (“Abacus”), a financial services company specializing in alternative asset management, with a focus on longevity-based assets and personalized financial planning, today announced a partnership with Retirable Inc. (“Retirable”), an SEC-registered retirement planning platform built for everyday Americans, to connect Abacus clients with personalized retirement planning.


Abacus works with policyholders at a pivotal moment, when they are deciding what to do with one of their largest assets. This partnership gives those clients a clear next step. Once a client’s policy decision is complete, Abacus and its insurance affiliates will introduce them to Retirable’s licensed fiduciary advisors through dedicated channels, including warm transfers and scheduled introductions, so the conversation about what comes next can start right away.


Abacus will also integrate its AI-powered lifespan modeling technology, Abacus LifeARC™, into the Retirable platform, marking an expansion into new client channels. Abacus LifeARC™ is built on 20 years of proprietary insights. It generates lifespan projections that Retirable’s advisors can use, alongside other planning inputs, to inform retirement income and legacy planning for the everyday retirees and pre-retirees Retirable serves.


“Everyone planning for retirement wants to know how long their savings need to last,” said Jay Jackson, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Abacus. “Through this partnership, our clients will have a direct path to Retirable's advisors when they are ready to ask. Abacus LifeARC™, our intelligence layer, will give those advisors a personalized view of the answer, and bring it to a much broader set of households. Together, we can help more people plan for the life they'll actually live.”


“We approach retirement planning with the goal of helping people make confident decisions with the resources they have, and longevity is one of the most talked about pieces of that equation,” said Tyler End, CEO and co-founder of Retirable. “Integrating LifeARC™ into our planning process gives our advisors another powerful tool to help clients think more personally about how long their money needs to last, how much they can comfortably spend, and what they want to leave behind. Pairing Abacus’s longevity insights with our personalized, human guidance will help us build even more informed retirement plans for our clients, and give them the confidence they deserve.”

**About Abacus**


Abacus Global Management (NYSE: ABX) is a financial services company specializing in alternative asset management, data-driven wealth solutions, technology innovation, and institutional services. With a focus on longevity-based assets and personalized financial planning, Abacus leverages proprietary data analytics and decades of industry expertise to deliver innovative solutions that optimize financial outcomes for individuals and institutions worldwide.


For more information, please visit[www.abacusgm.com](http://www.abacusgm.com/)


**About Retirable**


Retirable is the first holistic retirement solution built for everyday Americans with the ongoing care of an advisor, offering services across retirement investing, planning and spending. Combining licensed financial advisors with intelligent automation, Retirable helps users turn their savings into reliable income, create custom retirement plans and navigate every stage of retirement with confidence. Founded in 2019 by industry veterans Tyler End and Ian Yamey, Retirable has helped thousands of Americans retire smarter, with over $175M in assets under management and counting. Retirable is headquartered in NYC and backed by investors like Nationwide Ventures, Western & Southern Financial Group, Vestigo Ventures and Primary Venture Partners.
